coordinate_frame: Origin at the centre of the northeast gable on the measured ground footprint. X points northwest across its facade. Y follows the ridge southwest, Z points up. The White Chapel shares the northwest boundary for part of its length.
confidence: The overall height is the coarse source value, which includes both wings. Eave, intermediate elevations and widths are estimates proportioned against the source measurements and oblique archive views.

evidence.visibility: The northeast hall gable has five narrow upper lights with staggered pointed heads, five lower rectangular lights, a wide stone transom, recessed arched door and one high narrow vent. The photograph also resolves the two circles on its adjoining southeast long wall. The streetwise positions and dimensions are estimated.

source_contact.facade_treatment: Keep the shared span plain and preserve the remaining independent chapel as original source geometry.

less_visible_faces: The southwest gable and an upper series of pointed bays are visible in the early wide view. The exact door joinery, upper subdivision of the end window and the covered lower openings are estimates. The small northern chapel and scientific building have independent outlines.
